state.persona: First-time visitor going through MERIDIAN's 5-step onboarding on desktop.
state.jtbd: Tell MERIDIAN what kind of traveler I am and how public my profile should be.
state.step_1: '1 / 5 What kind of traveler are you — this week?' Five large option cards: Family, Couple, Solo, Work layover, Friends, each with a one-line description. Bottom: 'Skip and enter World' (text) and [CONTINUE] (button, always enabled).
state.observed_after_click: User clicks the 'Solo' card. Measured computed style: every card, including Solo, keeps the identical 1px faint border; no aria-pressed or checkmark; nothing visibly changes. Same on step 5 (Private / Discoverable): the chosen card looks identical to the unchosen one.
state.continue_behavior: CONTINUE advances even when nothing is selected.
state.refresh_behavior: At step 3/5 the user refreshes; the page returns to '1 / 5' (their earlier answers are silently kept in storage but the step counter restarts).
state.back_behavior: At step 2/5 the browser Back button leaves onboarding entirely and returns to the previous page; there is no in-flow Back control.

can_tell_selected.instructions: After clicking 'Solo', can the user tell which option is selected?

privacy_choice_confidence.instructions: On step 5, can the user be confident whether they chose Private or Discoverable before clicking Enter World?

refresh_understood.instructions: After the refresh returns to step 1, would the user understand their earlier answers are still saved?

criteria: Broken: user cannot tell what they chose or where they are

legend.0: Broken: user cannot tell what they chose or where they are
